_meta.description: Known mistakes/lessons for xedit. New entries only get added via ChangeGate's approve() (change_gate.py) -- never edited by hand as a shortcut around review.

patterns.whatToLookFor: Trying to run FO4Edit (xFOEdit64.exe) unattended with -autoload -script ... -autoexit: it still opened a modal window and sat idle (2 s CPU, never ran the script), so an overnight or scripted check never finishes.
patterns.correction: For headless validation use xDump64.exe from the same xEdit folder: `xDump64.exe -FO4 -D:<data folder>\ -check MyPlugin.esp` prints every record error and exits; without -check it dumps every field decoded, which is a good way to confirm hand-built records (VMAD, quest stages/objectives, placed refs) decode as intended. Point -D at a temp folder holding Fallout4.esm + Strings\Fallout4_en.* + the plugin when the plugin lives in an MO2 mod folder.

patterns.whatToLookFor: xEdit's message pane shows: "[PACK:FE0C74E3] has invalid ObjectID 0044E3 for a light module. You will not be able to save this file with the ESL flag active." A plugin flagged ESL (light) can only use FormIDs from 000800 to 000FFF. Records numbered outside that range break the ESL flag.
patterns.correction: Either renumber the records into the 000800-000FFF range (xEdit: right-click the plugin, "Compact FormIDs for ESL") or remove the ESL flag and keep it as a normal plugin. Make a backup first, because FormIDs referenced by other plugins or saves will change.

patterns.whatToLookFor: xEdit's message pane shows: "<Warning: Modules with extended FormID range should always have the Game Master as their first master.>" The plugin uses the extended (light) FormID range, but Fallout4.esm is not listed first in its masters.
patterns.correction: Open the plugin's header, check the Masters list, and make sure Fallout4.esm is the first master. In xEdit, right-click the plugin and choose "Sort Masters". Then save the file.

patterns.whatToLookFor: xEdit's message pane shows: "Background Loader: Error: record REFR contains unexpected (or out of order) subrecord XPWR". The same error shows up for SCEN records with subrecord DTID. Some record in a plugin has a subrecord in the wrong place, or one this game's record definition doesn't expect.
patterns.correction: The plugin was probably saved by a tool that wrote the subrecords wrongly, or made for a different version. Open the plugin in xEdit and look at the flagged record, then re-save it in the Creation Kit or ask the mod author for a fixed version. If it's your own mod, remove the stray subrecord and check the file again. Don't clean or delete records until you know which plugin is affected.
